# Warrant

> A decision record for AI agents: signed, hash-addressed, with reasons you can
> re-run. When an agent accepts, rejects or proposes something it writes a small
> JSON record saying **what** was decided, **under** which policy (pinned by the
> hash of its exact bytes), **because** of which reasons, on **which** evidence.
> The record's hash is its identity, so nothing can be quietly edited afterwards.

This file exists because reviewers kept reporting things that were not true. Four
model reviews in four days filed findings that were artefacts of not knowing what
they were looking at — files "missing" that were on `master` while the reviewer
read a feature branch, a tool "printing 33/33" read out of an archived evidence
blob, a "three-week" sibling pin that was same-day. A fifth session spent 785,000
tokens reading and produced no finding at all. None of them were careless. They
were oriented badly, and that was this repository's fault, not theirs.

So: read this before concluding anything.

## Orient yourself first

- **`master` is the only thing in force.** Everything on a branch is a candidate:
  readable, citable, **not adopted**. Check the ref before reporting anything
  absent — that single mistake accounts for most false findings here.
- **Present is not adopted.** A document existing on a branch, or even on
  `master`, says nothing about its governance status. Location is a fact about
  git; adoption is a threshold warrant signed by roster keys, recorded in
  `.warrants/`, never a commit message and never a heading.
- [MAP.md](MAP.md): generated from git — for every document this repository
  cites, which ref actually holds it. Several live in the sibling repository
  `sigma-glyph`, and the map says which branch.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): conduct rules. Rules 1–5 are in force; 6–7 are marked
  DRAFT and are not.

## Check anything in one command

Nothing here asks to be believed. Every claim below is one command away, offline,
no account:

```bash
python3 tools/check.py                  # everything, one verdict
```

That runs all 28 checks the repository's claims rest on and prints one line. A
check that could not run — Go not built, oracle missing — is reported UNRUN with
its own exit status, never as passed: a harness printing ALL PASS while silently
skipping the Go suites would be claiming two implementations agreed on the
strength of never having asked one of them.

Individual pieces, if you want them:

```bash
python3 impl/warrant.py selftest        # ALL PASS
python3 impl/warrant.py conformance     # ALL PASS (45/45)
python3 tests/differential.py           # ALL AGREE  — Python vs Go, byte-exact
python3 tests/negative.py               # ALL AGREE  — MUST-REJECT vectors
python3 tools/repo_map.py --check-map   # every cited document is located
```

If a document and a command disagree, **the command is right**. Two files in this
repository were wrong about their own test counts and PyPI status until they were
caught; the fix was to generate the numbers rather than type them.

## Interoperating with the provenance world

This format was an island: a reader with in-toto, SLSA, Sigstore or Rekor tooling
could do nothing with a warrant record. `tools/intoto.py` expresses a decision as
an **in-toto Statement v1** so the stack sits *on* that ecosystem rather than
beside it — in-toto says what happened to an artefact, a warrant says who was
allowed to decide it and on which re-runnable reasons.

```bash
python3 tools/intoto.py wrap <WarrantID>        # Statement on stdout
python3 tools/intoto.py check <statement.json>  # does it bind to this store?
```

`check` recomputes every digest against the store rather than validating a
schema: a Statement can be perfectly well-formed and describe a record that does
not exist, and a bridge must not pass that through. Ten tamper cases are pinned.

Two honest limits. The Statement is **not signed** here — DSSE wrapping and Rekor
submission are separate steps with separate trust, deliberately not hidden inside
a converter. And the `predicateType` lives under
`github.com/s0fractal/warrant`, a URI this project controls; an external audit
proposed `warrant.dev`, which it does not own, and minting a type under someone
else's namespace is a false claim about who defines it.

## The specification

- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): the format. §5.1 key state, §6 verification, §7 settlement,
  §9 multi-root stores, §11 the `warrant.verify-report@v0` machine boundary, §12
  trust configuration, §13 registries, §14 media type and schemas. Deliberately
  boring — implementable in a day, and any two implementations must agree
  byte-exact on every WarrantID.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed per release, and — the part that
  trips reviewers — which of the **four** version numbers moved. The body version,
  the SPEC document version, the report tag and the package version are different
  numbers and are routinely read as one. Everything before 2026-07-30 is
  reconstructed after the fact and says so.
- `schemas/`: published JSON Schema for the body, envelope, verify report, trust
  config and evidence-pack manifest. Passing a schema is **necessary and not
  sufficient** — no schema can express canonicalization, signature acceptance,
  re-execution or settlement, and `tools/schema_check.py` prints the classes it
  cannot express rather than leaving them implied.
- [profiles/eu-ai-act-article-12.md](profiles/eu-ai-act-article-12.md): mapping to
  the EU AI Act record-keeping clause, with its gaps stated in the same document.
- Three implementations that agree on every vector: `impl/` (Python), `impl-go/`,
  `impl-rs/` (no third-party crates, own SHA-256 and Ed25519). All three now also
  agree on whether a **store** verifies, on broken stores as well as clean ones —
  see the base-grade limit under the gaps below.

## If you are reviewing this project

Read [sigma-glyph/reviews/README.md](https://github.com/s0fractal/sigma-glyph/blob/master/reviews/README.md)
for the protocol, and `reviews/` here for the 74 prior reviews so you do not
rediscover settled points.

Four things that will save you a wasted pass:

1. **Running the green suites is not a review.** They are green. Every real
   finding here was green-and-still-broken; saying "suites pass" will be rejected
   (AGENTS.md §3).
2. **A finding is a reproduction, not a sentence.** Counter-vectors are executed
   against a pinned commit by `tools/adversarial_gate.py`. Anything that does not
   run is a Question — an honest and useful category, but not a finding.
3. **Write blocks that can fail.** The commonest defect in submitted
   counter-vectors here is a block that reports a violation whatever the machine
   does: asserting the *correct* behaviour and then printing VIOLATION, or
   printing it in every branch of an if/else. Three separate reviewers did this,
   and so did the author of the check that catches it.
4. **Say what you did not examine.** It is worth more than a confident sweep.

## Where the honest gaps are

Stated here so you do not have to find them, and because a project about
verifiable provenance that hides its own open items is arguing against itself:

- **No independent gate is currently available.** The reviewing families are
  unaffordable or restricted, so items land UNGATED under a recorded attestation
  naming who took responsibility. `policies/gate-settlement.json` defines that
  state; it is disclosed rather than dressed up as a passed gate.
- **WRT-002 is design-only** and carries open findings from three reviewer
  families plus one confirmed here on 2026-07-29 (a quorum authorised only by a
  losing policy branch could adopt a root — fixed, with the negative control run).
- **`settle.py` reports UNRESOLVED about itself**: claims raised against
  superseded revisions that were never re-run to a decision. It says so rather
  than assuming its own fixes.
- Part of the Lean chain rests transitively on `native_decide`, which puts the
  compiler in the trusted base.
- **`cmd@v1` verdicts are trusted, by specification.** SPEC §7 states the
  verifier does not re-execute them — their trust model is the container. So a
  `cmd@v1` outcome fingerprint carries the verdict its filer wrote, and the
  re-litigation novelty test can be satisfied by writing a different word. The
  same hole was closed for `ski@v1`, where re-execution is available and the
  re-run verdict is now what the fingerprint records. This one is a limit of the
  format, not of the code, and it is stated rather than patched over.
- **Multi-root stores (§9) are verified only as far as root admission.** The
  threshold rule that gates adoption is exercised, including that an unbound key
  claiming an actor does not satisfy it. Deeper §9 behaviour is not covered by a
  vector here.
- **`impl-rs` verifies stores at SPEC §6 BASE grade only** — no settlement, no
  key state, no trust config, and `ski@v1` reasons are reported
  `ski@v1 unverified: runtime unavailable` because it has no oracle. Three-way
  parity is therefore a claim about base-grade verification, tested in
  `tests/verify_three_way.py` on nine deliberately broken stores; settlement-grade
  parity remains Python against Go.

## Reporting a defect

[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — what is in scope, what is a documented limit rather
than a defect, and the severity ladder. It also says plainly what the response
capacity is: one maintainer and one model actor, no security team, no promised
fix timeline. A reproduction that exits non-zero on the defect and zero once
fixed becomes a permanent regression test.

## Optional

- [PRIOR-ART.md](PRIOR-ART.md): defensive publication record — Software Heritage
  archival, timestamped disclosure manifests, and a plain statement of what a
  timestamp does and does not prove.
- [TRADEMARK.md](TRADEMARK.md): licences stay permissive; conformance claims are
  tied to passing the published vectors.
- [MODEL-ACTORS.md](MODEL-ACTORS.md): model actors hold roster keys here; what
  that protects and what it explicitly does not claim.
- [standards/CEN-JTC21-contribution.md](standards/CEN-JTC21-contribution.md):
  draft contribution on third-party verifiability of agent decision records.
